sanskrit: aparā cāpi kolaṃbā mahāśaktiḥ sanātanī | kolarūpī yayāviṣṭaḥ keśavaścojjahāra gām || 27 || tasmātsā viṣṇunā coktā kolaṃbeti stutārcitā | sā ca devī mayā pārtha bhaktiyogena toṣitā || 28 || vārāhagirisaṃsthā māṃ samānītā ca sābravīt | yatrāhaṃ nārada sadā tiṣṭhāmi kṛpayārthinām || 29 ||
english: 27-33. Another great Śakti is the eternal Kolaṃbā. Keśava in the form of a Boar (‘Kola’) was entered into by her and he lifted up the Earth. Hence she was called Kolaṃbā by Viṣṇu and then eulogized and adored. O son of Pṛthā, that goddess was pleased by me by the Yoga of devotion. She who was on the mountain Varāha Giri was brought by me. She said to me: “There must be a Kūpa (‘well’) presided over by Rudrāṇī in the place where I stay, due to the kindness towards the suppliants. Without that well, I do not find any pleasure anywhere. Hence, O Brāhmaṇa, dig an excellent well yourself here.”
